ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and authorised signatories against the Luxembourg consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the European Union financial sanctions list, and, for any USD-clearing, the OFAC SDN list. PEPs are subject to enhanced due diligence, including senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. All screenings must be documented, risk-scored and retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - online platform at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The commercial name must be written in Latin characters. Accepted languages include French, German, Luxembourgish, or any language transliterated into Latin script. The name must conclude with the mention 'société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The name must not be contrary to public policy, misleading, or vulnerable to confusion with existing names in the same register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may re-file a corrected name online or request a formal written reason from the Luxembourg Business Registers. If rejected again, an administrative appeal must be filed with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification, represented by a Luxembourg-licensed attorney. The appeal should include the proposed name and evidence of non-conflict with prior registrations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted only if it corresponds to a physical address in Luxembourg where official documents can be served and where the books and records, statutory registers, and minutes of the SCSp are kept. For the wholesale used heavy machinery industry, a virtual office without local substantive staff and a local authorised representative will be regarded as substance-light, leading to enhanced AML scrutiny and possible tax re-assessment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 101-1 to 101-8 govern the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; applicable RCS filing rules under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and Grand-Ducal Regulation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Partnership (Contrat de Société) filed with the RCS, accompanied by the appropriate RCS registration form and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital for an SCSp; contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement. There is no statutory escrow account requirement unless the partnership agreement itself imposes a contribution escrow or lock-up provision.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation of the SCSp be and is hereby ratified, and the partnership agreement as presented is approved. RESOLVED, that the subscription of partnership interests described in the contribution schedule is accepted, and contributions are deemed subscribed in full. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [address], Luxembourg, and the general partner [name] is appointed with sole authority to manage, represent and bind the partnership. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed as manager and that any partner signing this resolution, together with the appointed compliance officer, is authorized to file the partnership deed, the RCS application, the beneficial ownership declaration, and all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS, online via LBR.business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through LBR.business indicating the proposed corporate name, the SCSp legal form, and the intended object. The name must be unique, identify the legal form, and be consistent with Luxembourg legal order. Await the name reservation certificate before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all partners or their authorized representatives
Proposed object statement aligned with ISIC 4659
Certificate of non-dissolution and Registry extract if any corporate partner exists
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to identity or misleading character, submit a fresh request with three alternative names and a memorandum distinguishing the chosen name from existing RCS entries; an internal review may be requested within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary office if notarization is elected or required; otherwise executing partners; subsequent filing with RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Contrat de Société setting out the corporate object (wholesale remarketing of second-hand construction excavators and rollers), registered office in Luxembourg, identity of the general partner, contribution schedule, profit-sharing arrangements, management powers, and dissolution triggers. Execute the deed either by notarial act or by private written agreement signed by all partners. If real property forms part of the contributions, notarization shall be mandatory.
required_dossiers: Consent of the registered office address provider
Notarial deed, if real property contribution or notarization is elected
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS objects to the contractual wording, convene the partners to adopt a supplementary agreement amending the contested articles, then re-execute and re-file the amended deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg or EEA credit institution; RCS registration follows upon confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the SCSp and effect the agreed contributions in cash or in kind. No minimum capital is required by law, but the contribution schedule must be performed as stipulated in the partnership agreement. Obtain the bank confirmation letter evidencing the deposit or the documented valuation of in-kind contributions.
required_dossiers: Contribution confirmation letter or in-kind valuation report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the file due to AML concerns, supplement the KYC information with a beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds evidence; request the bank's internal AML review or proceed with a different licensed institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS, online via LBR.business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration application through the LBR portal, attaching the executed partnership agreement, name reservation certificate, bank contribution confirmation, registered office consent, identification of general and limited partners, and the list of managers authorized to represent the SCSp. Pay the applicable registration fee. Upon internal verification, the RCS issues the registration extract and assigns the corporate registration number.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership preliminary declaration and partner identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or suspended, rectify the flagged elements through LBR.business within the prescribed cure period, or submit a formal explanation addressing the registrar's concerns; in the event of rejection, file an amended application with corrected attachments and a cover statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and Beneficial Ownership Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the registration and partnership deed are transmitted automatically to RESA for official publication. Concurrently, the SCSp must file a complete beneficial ownership declaration before the deadline, identifying every individual directly or indirectly owning or controlling the partnership. Upon completion, obtain the RESA publication confirmation and the final RCS extract.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all beneficial owners
Ownership chart for layered corporate structures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed, request expeditious handling from LBR; if the beneficial ownership declaration is late, submit the declaration immediately with a petition for reduction of any assessed administrative penalty, invoking good-faith compliance and prompt remediation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Energy (Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale de l'Industrie et de l'Énergie)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: N/A – No sector-specific operating license is required for wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators under ISIC 4659; an Autorisation d'Établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011 may become relevant only if a local permanent commercial establishment is created.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for pure wholesale storage and trading of used machinery; a Category B registration may apply if warehousing facilities exceed specified thresholds or if any mechanical treatment, washing, or maintenance activity is introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge in pure trading operations; if maintenance or cleaning activities are added, treated wastewater must comply with Grand-Ducal Regulations on industrial discharges and VOCs must remain below 50 mg C/Nm³ in any solvent-using process. Used hydraulic oils and fluids must be stored in bunded, impermeable containers and removed by a certified waste carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for any warehouse or office premises; structural load inspection by a licensed engineer covering machine storage floors; workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for electrical installations, emergency exits, lifting equipment, and hazard communication.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) — Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority; official integrated tax and administrative portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — determine whether the foreign entity has a Luxembourg permanent establishment or taxable nexus; if not, appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative before making supplies. Step 2 — register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via MyGuichet; the RCS filing establishes the Luxembourg business matricule. Step 3 — obtain or confirm the national tax number with the ACD; non-resident partners are not required to hold a Luxembourg TIN merely as partners of a transparent SCSp unless they have a Luxembourg permanent establishment or derive Luxembourg-source income. Step 4 — register for VAT with the AED using the electronic VAT registration application or Form 1, attaching the partnership agreement, RCS certificate, foreign registration certificate, general partner/managers' identity documents, proof of economic activity and KYC/AML files. Step 5 — ensure VAT registration is effective before the first taxable supply or import; for non-EU principals without a Luxembourg establishment, appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative where required. Step 6 — obtain a Luxembourg EORI number for customs operations and, if the SCSp makes intra-EU supplies, ensure the VAT number is valid for EC sales list reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg direct tax purposes; it is not itself subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax, and profits are allocated and taxed at partner level. For Luxembourg VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is a separate taxable person where it carries out an economic activity, and it must be registered in its own name for VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a US-style check-the-box election. Transparency is the statutory default for the SCSp, and no general unilateral election is available to subject the SCSp to corporate income tax unless a narrow statutory option applies in situations where all partners are fully taxable corporate taxpayers and the conditions are strictly met. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralised under the Luxembourg provisions implementing EU ATAD, including deduction/no-inclusion, double deduction and imported mismatch rules. An advance tax agreement or ruling with the ACD may be used to obtain binding confirmation of the entity's classification and to document the absence of a hybrid mismatch where a partner jurisdiction characterises the SCSp differently.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the amended Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold applies to non-resident traders: Luxembourg VAT registration is required before the first taxable supply unless the reverse-charge mechanism transfers liability to the Luxembourg customer. A domestic small-enterprise franchise exemption is available only to Luxembourg-established taxable persons whose annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 excluding Luxembourg VAT; a used-heavy-machinery wholesale exporter will ordinarily exceed or not qualify for that exemption, so full VAT registration is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no mandatory B2B electronic invoicing, no real-time fiscal clearance, no API transmission of every invoice to the tax authority, and no digital stamping regime. VAT invoices may be issued on paper or electronically if authenticity, integrity and legibility are preserved. For sales to Luxembourg public entities, suppliers must transmit PEPPOL BIS 3.0/BII-compliant electronic invoices through certified access points under EU Directive 2014/55/EU. The AED accepts electronic filing of VAT returns through MyGuichet and may require SAF-T-type electronic data during audits. Future continuous transaction controls may be introduced under the EU VAT in the Digital Age initiative, but are not yet in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A sale of used construction excavators from Luxembourg to a customer outside the EU is eligible for the 0% export VAT rate if the following cumulative conditions are met: (i) the goods are supplied by a taxable person acting as such; (ii) the excavators are physically dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU; (iii) the export is made in the seller's name or on the seller's account, or the seller holds sufficient evidence of the physical exit of the specific machines; (iv) the export is supported by a valid customs export declaration in Luxembourg or in the Member State of exit and, when required, transit or re-export documentation; and (v) the seller maintains a complete audit trail from acquisition to destination, including bill of lading/CMR/airway bill, insurance, payment, and inward remittance. The zero rate also covers certain services directly linked to the export, and, under general place-of-supply rules, services supplied to non-EU business customers who are established outside Luxembourg and do not effectively use the services in Luxembourg. For intra-EU supplies to another EU taxable person, zero-rating applies only if the buyer's valid EU VAT identification number is obtained and the goods physically move to the other Member State, with the supply reported in the EC sales list.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document/EAD) accepted in the Member State of exit
Bill of Lading for ocean transport, CMR consignment note for road transport, or Air Waybill for air transport evidencing physical dispatch from the EU
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list describing serial numbers, model, engine/chassis numbers and condition of each used excavator
Purchase invoice and title chain evidencing lawful acquisition of the used machinery
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 showing receipt of the export proceeds from the non-EU buyer within 180 days
Customs release or import certificate at destination, or equivalent official evidence of arrival where obtainable
Transport order, insurance certificate and any transit declaration (e.g. T1) supporting the export route
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are treated as high risk. The AED may, in audit, verify the customs declaration, physical routing, counterparty, VAT status, economic substance of the SCSp, and actual repatriation of proceeds. If the exporter fails to substantiate export or FX repatriation within the required time, the supply is retrospectively recharacterised as a taxable Luxembourg supply; VAT becomes due at 17% of the agreed consideration, plus late-payment interest, and input VAT credits or refunds previously granted are clawed back. Administrative fines may be imposed up to the amount of tax evaded, and deliberate or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger criminal tax fraud proceedings with substantial monetary fines and imprisonment. The limitation period for reassessment is generally five years but is extended to ten years in cases of VAT fraud. The SCSp's general partner and the managers who knowingly signed or caused false export documentation may be held jointly and severally liable for the reinstated VAT, fines and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for financial-sector conduct and AML/CFT supervision; the BCL oversees the national balance-of-payments statistical system and acts as Eurosystem member for monetary policy and payment systems.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area Member State with full current-account and capital-account convertibility pursuant to Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no exchange-control approvals, no transaction-level licensing, and no restrictions on profit remittance or capital repatriation. Practical hurdles arise exclusively from EU restrictive measures (e.g., Council Regulation 833/2014 sanctions), CSSF AML/CFT obligations under the amended Law of 12 November 2004, and the BCL's statistical reporting regime: residents must report cross-border payments and claims/liabilities above de minimis thresholds (BCL Regulation 2013/01 and related circulars). The SCSp must file monthly/quarterly balance-of-payments returns to the BCL for every cross-border flow exceeding the mandatory reporting threshold, and must retain underlying trade and counterparty documentation for verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no compulsory surrender, no mandatory conversion to EUR, and no statutory repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency in any bank account. However, the SCSp must comply with (i) BCL balance-of-payments reporting for each export-related inflow, (ii) EU Intrastat declarations for intra-EU dispatches when annual goods flow thresholds are met, and (iii) customs/EORI obligations under the Union Customs Code for extra-EU exports. Invoicing currency is unrestricted; EUR, USD, and CNY settlement are all permitted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account; USD Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (subscription/capital-call) and Operational Account
Operational EUR Account; Documentary Trade Account (LC issuance/advising)
Operational Current Account with multi-currency sweep

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Wealth Management Account (not recommended for trade operations)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. Luxembourg-authorized EMIs (e.g., PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie S.C.A., Paysafe entities) are supervised by the CSSF and can provide euro IBANs and low-value payment services, but they do not offer commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, or committed lines — rail types essential for used-heavy-machinery trading. Cross-border offshore EMIs (UK, Lithuania, Singapore, Hong Kong) are legally able to maintain multi-currency accounts for an SCSp, but most Luxembourg banks will reject them as counterparty or transit accounts for outbound trade because of heightened third-party risk and lack of Luxembourg supervision. EMIs are acceptable only for minor operational expenses (legal fees, subscriptions), never for invoiced machinery settlements. Any EMI must undergo independent KYC equivalence review and must not be the sole treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted in principle under CSSF Circular 17/650 governing video-identification and electronic signatures, but top-tier Luxembourg banks impose stricter internal policies. In practice, at least one authorized signatory or the SCSp's designated general partner must attend an in-person kick-off interview at the bank's Luxembourg office if any ultimate beneficial owner is a non-EEA resident or if the transaction flows involve non-EEA high-risk jurisdictions. Board members located in the EU can often complete onboarding remotely with apostilled constitutional documents, certified passport copies, and notarized powers of attorney. For this SCSp with non-resident ownership, the safe execution path assumes one in-person interview per legal entity at each banking relationship initiation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp structuring involving non-EEA UBOs with multi-layered ownership; bank flags opacity and lack of economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain with individual identity docs; registered office and substance evidence (lease, local administrator agreement); SCSp partnership agreement (LLP agreement) with capital account schedule; audited or accountant-certified management accounts; a written business rationale memo describing the used-machinery remarketing model and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade flows to/from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Russia/Belarus since EU Council Regulation 833/2014, Syria, Iran) for end-use of excavators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-use and end-user certificates from the final buyer; serial-number-level equipment lists; customs export declarations (EXA); transport contracts (CMR / Bill of Lading); Incoterms 2020 on each invoice; an internal sanctions-screening procedure demonstrating negative hits for all counterparties and vessels/entities involved; contractual re-export prohibitions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Price mismatches between broker invoice, auction sale, and bank transfer (over- or under-invoicing risk frequent in secondhand machinery).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent valuation reports (e.g., SGS, CERA, or Ritchie Bros. auction results); original purchase invoice from the prior owner; condition reports and equipment photos with hours/odometer; insurance valuation certificates; a written transfer-pricing or arm's-length justification with comparable transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments arranged through intermediaries in another jurisdiction (e.g., supplier in China, agent in Dubai) without clear documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written agency/intermediary agreements; full chain of correspondence evidencing commercial rationale; bank confirmation of ultimate beneficiary; pro-forma invoices matching final invoice value; no unnamed nominee or bearer instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow injections from investors where source-of-wealth evidence is incomplete or investor wealth located in financial-secrecy jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices and escrow agreements; bank statements of the investor for the last 12 months; investor tax returns or audited financials; personal/corporate net-worth statements signed under penalty; clear chain from divestment/liquidity event to the transfer into the SCSp account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must flow via SWIFT MT103 with explicit purpose code 'CAPT' (capital contribution) or 'INVS' (investment), referencing 'SCSp capital call' in the remittance information field. Each transfer must be tied to a written capital call notice stating the investor's capital account in the SCSp. Banks require a source-of-funds declaration for each investor above EUR 10,000 and full UBO documentation before first credit. The funds may be received in a dedicated Capital Escrow Account (at Banque de Luxembourg or BIL) and then transferred to the operating account under the partnership agreement's lock-up provisions. BCL balance-of-payments reporting must classify the inflow as 'PF - direct investment - capital contribution'. No exchange-control declaration is required, but banks may reject transfers from jurisdictions listed on FATF grey lists unless the investor provides enhanced due diligence evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements must be layered by ticket size and counterparty confidence. Standard supplier settlements use SWIFT MT103 (payment for goods, purpose code 'GDSV' or 'TRAD') with invoice and transport reference in the remittance field. For purchases above EUR 500,000 or new suppliers, an irrevocable Confirmed Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700 issued by BNP Paribas Luxembourg / BIL / Société Générale Luxembourg; MT707 for amendments) is recommended, with documents against payment (D/P) as a fallback. For high-risk destinations, use a Standby LC (MT760) to secure performance. All outbound disbursements must be pre-screened against EU sanctions and the bank's targeted financial sanctions list; copies of the LC, invoice, insurance (ICC-A), and bill of lading must be retained for BCL balance-of-payments reporting. The SCSp must maintain an EORI number (LU-based) for customs declarations and apply Invoice/Contract/ Transport (CIT) coherence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forwards (up to 24-month maturity) against EUR for USD, CNY, and JPY trade settlements
FX Swaps (roll-over of forward positions) for interim liquidity alignment
Currency Options (purchased calls/puts on USD/EUR and EUR/CNH; premium-paid structure only — no short options)
Offshore RMB Non-Deliverable Forwards (CNY/CNH NDFs) where onshore CNY settlement is not permissible or insufficiently liquid
Cross-Currency Swaps (for any non-EUR borrowing or long-dated asset exposure, subject to EMIR margin thresholds)
Plain Vanilla FX Spot overlay executed through the banking counterparty for immediate settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filing and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by partners within 6 months of fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for calendar-year accounting); filing and publication in the RCS/electronic companies register within 1 month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 per late filing; repeated defaults trigger formal notice, publication sanctions, and ultimately compulsory strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; also to be updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to EUR 125,000 for the entity and EUR 1,250–125,000 for the managing partner; criminal sanctions for obstruction and prohibition on distributions in case of persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax return for sociétés de personnes (SCSp collective income declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Paper return due by 31 March of the following fiscal year; electronic extensions normally granted to 31 December of the following year; partners' individual tax filings follow the partnership allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties from EUR 100 to EUR 10,000; automatic 10% late filing surcharge on assessed income; where no return is filed, the ACD may issue an ex officio assessment and impose criminal penalties for wilful non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is required when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following threshold criteria for two consecutive years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50 employees. A partner request or public-interest status also triggers audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements of public-interest entities or by voluntary election to the extent authorized.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file an RBE annual confirmation by 31 March even when no beneficial-owner data has changed. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in UBO attendance requires a supplementary RBE update within 30 days of the event, thereby ensuring the electronic register is continuously aligned; the managing partner remains accountable for the accuracy of the declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / Managing Partners (Registre des gérants)

stage_6.entry_description: State the fiscal year (e.g., 31.12.2025) and RCS/matricule of the SCSp; identification of the fiscal-transparency status.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident general/limited partners must quote their Luxembourg tax number if a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists; otherwise rely on treaty allocation.
